page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor, operating at a clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores placing the instance in the top 25% of tested hardware. It demonstrates high efficiency in cryptographic and mathematical operations, supported by hardware flags such as AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and FMA. Memory performance is highly polarized: cached small-block read bandwidth is exceptionally strong at 4132.73 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations are highly efficient, with Redis achieving 61.81 million operations per second.

Given its compute-heavy resource density and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.c7a.16xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, image processing, ray tracing, and database operations. It also supports moderate machine learning workloads, showing strong performance in prompt processing and text generation for small LLM models, though performance drops to average levels for medium 7B models.

Benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU performance, high cached memory bandwidth, and excellent database and Redis SET operation speeds. This hardware profile is highly efficient for compute-bound tasks, multi-threaded decompression, image processing, and database operations that do not require local SSD storage.
